order_note: No predecessor and no order on this engine. SQL 134 needs public.loss_draft_tracking with total_escrowed, draw_amount_requested, draw_stage, draw_amount_released and holdback_amount, public.loss_draft_releases with loss_draft_id, draw_number, amount_requested, amount_released, release_date, released_at, status, notes and created_by (restored Supabase schema, supabase/migrations/20260308163837_*.sql), both owned by checksops_admin, and the roles checksops and authenticated. The Loss Draft API change (#1464, aws/functions/api/workflow-rpc.mjs loss_draft_action: mark_escrowed, request_draw, record_release, record_holdback, mark_final_release; owner decision 2026-10-30) updates those five loss_draft_tracking columns (with escrow_status, check_received_date and updated_at, which SQL 50 already grants to checksops and authenticated) and, for record_release, inserts the draw into loss_draft_releases (id from gen_random_uuid(), no sequence). No migration in this repository grants UPDATE on those five columns or INSERT on loss_draft_releases (SQL 50 does not; SQL 51 revokes SQL 50's loss_draft_tracking grants where it is run), so PostgreSQL refuses those writes before row-level security. The policies aws_write_loss_draft_tracking (aws_can_write_check(check_intake_item_id)) and aws_write_loss_draft_releases (aws/rls/sql/24_complete_write_policies.sql: aws_can_write_claim of the draft's claim_id) stay the authorization boundary and are not changed: a draft without a claim_id still gets no Draws row (the API reports release_recorded false). SQL 134 grants exactly those column privileges to checksops and authenticated and changes nothing else. If the read-only inspect finds both lines on all fourteen columns already held it reports already_applied true and nothing is applied (the pin is then recorded as verified live, not applied). No later migration revokes these grants. The API change itself is deployed through the guarded Lambda path, not by this pin.
